title: Radial profiles of lensed z ∼ 1 galaxies on sub-kiloparsec scales
question: What are the radial profiles and exponential scale lengths of the star formation rate, stellar mass, molecular gas mass, and dust mass surface densities in two strongly lensed galaxies at z ~ 1 on sub-kiloparsec scales, and how do they compare to local and other high-redshift galaxies?

recipe.goal: Construct galactocentric radius masks in the image plane via gravitational lens modelling
recipe.method: Create concentric elliptical rings centred on the galaxy centre in the source plane, project the mask onto the image plane using the Lenstool gravitational lens model, and compute ring areas in the image plane
key_parameters: Ring width in image plane >= half the beam size (350 pc for CS HST, 400 pc for A521 HST, 300 pc for CS ALMA, 400 pc for A521 ALMA, 800 pc for CS SINFONI)
assumptions: Surface brightness is constant inside each ring and conserved through gravitational lensing

recipe.goal: Subtract foreground cluster galaxy contamination and extract radial HST photometry
recipe.method: Model bright foreground cluster members with a sum of two 2D Sersic profiles recursively and subtract them (or mask out overlapping galaxy with a 2-sigma contour ellipse in A521), then measure surface brightness in each elliptical ring across HST bands
key_parameters: 20 elliptical rings of 350 pc step (0 to 7 kpc) for Cosmic Snake; 20 elliptical rings of 400 pc step (0 to 8 kpc) for A521

recipe.goal: Fit FIR SED with modified black-body and derive radial dust mass and IR luminosity profiles
recipe.method: Fit a modified black-body (MBB) law over the integrated Herschel + ALMA rest-frame 650 um FIR SED of the Cosmic Snake, integrate from 8 to 1000 um for L_IR, and scale by ALMA 650 um continuum flux in 4 radial rings to get Sigma M_dust and ring L_IR
key_parameters: 4 rings of width 300 pc from 0 to 1.2 kpc; integration wavelength range 8 to 1000 um; observer-frame frequency 230 GHz
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_0 = 1.6 m^2 kg^-1; integrated MBB parameters (nu_0, beta, T_dust) are valid in each concentric ring; absorbed UV flux is reprocessed locally within the same ring

recipe.goal: Fit optical/NIR SEDs in radial rings to derive stellar mass and SFR surface densities
recipe.method: Fit HST multi-band photometry in each ring using the updated HyperZ code across 16 prior combinations to derive Sigma M_star, Sigma SFR, A_V, and L_IR; also fit integrated photometry of A521 counter-image
key_parameters: 16 prior combinations varying attenuation law (MW or Calzetti), Agemin (0.1 or 0.5 Gyr), A_V min (2, 3, or free), and SFH (constant or exponentially decreasing)
assumptions: Salpeter (1955) initial mass function; Lambda-CDM cosmology (H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7); constant magnification factor of 2.8 on A521 north-eastern counter-image

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas mass surface density radial profiles and integrated molecular gas masses from ALMA CO(4-3)
recipe.method: Create CO(4-3) moment-zero maps with CASA immoments, integrate CO(4-3) flux in concentric rings (and over counter-images for total masses), convert to L'_CO(4-3) and then to M_mol
key_parameters: 6 rings of width 300 pc up to 1.7 kpc (Cosmic Snake); 16 rings of width 400 pc up to 6 kpc (A521)
assumptions: CO luminosity ratio r_4,1 = L'_CO(4-3)/L'_CO(1-0) = 0.33; Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha_CO = 4.36 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; constant counter-image magnification factors of 4.3 (CS) and 2.8 (A521)

recipe.goal: Derive extinction-corrected H-alpha SFR surface density radial profile for the Cosmic Snake
recipe.method: Measure SINFONI H-alpha flux in 5 concentric rings, correct for dust extinction using the radial A_V profile from the HST SED fit, and convert H-alpha luminosity to SFR via the Kennicutt (1998) relation
key_parameters: 5 rings of width 800 pc from 0 to 4 kpc; Kennicutt (1998) conversion factor 1.26e41 erg s^-1 per M_sun yr^-1
assumptions: Milky Way attenuation law with k(6563 A)/R_V = 0.74

recipe.goal: Fit exponential scale lengths to radial profiles and compute half-light radii and stellar mass surface densities
recipe.method: Fit exponential functions to the radial profiles of Sigma M_star, Sigma SFR, Sigma M_mol, and Sigma M_dust to obtain scale lengths l; measure half-light radius (HLR) on lensing-corrected HST F160W counter-image radial profiles and compute Sigma M_star inside HLR (mu_star^HLR)
key_parameters: Fit over entire detection radius, plus inner 0 to 2.1 kpc fit for A521 Sigma M_mol before the spiral arm bump
assumptions: Radial surface density profiles follow an exponential decline

score_reason: Reduced maps are publicly archived at CDS, HST ring photometry is fully tabulated in the paper, and the analysis steps and conversion equations are explicitly written out; however, full end-to-end reproduction from images requires the Lenstool gravitational lens deflection maps and exact source-plane ellipse geometry, which are inherited from earlier papers.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data and CDS-archived reduced maps, clear mathematical definitions for M_mol, M_dust, and exponential scale lengths, and explicit quantitative answer keys in Tables 2, 3, and 4.
